background_story: Jericho was a rugged outdoorsman who spent most of his life exploring the wilderness along the Susquehanna River. Growing up in a small town near the river's banks, he developed a deep respect for the waterway and its history. As a young man, Jericho worked as a river guide, leading canoe trips and teaching people about the Susquehanna's rich cultural heritage. He became particularly fascinated with the Native American tribes that once thrived along the river, and spent years studying their traditions and ways of life. Jericho's love for the Susquehanna eventually led him to become a conservationist, working tirelessly to protect the river and its surrounding ecosystems from pollution and development. His dedication earned him the nickname 'Riverkeeper,' and he remained a steadfast guardian of the Susquehanna until his passing.
